solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: May be fired when her plans go awry

indicators.note: plans that go awry go wrong and fall apart, so the letters of these words fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A warning that a woman's schemes could misfire and get someone sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'May be fired' looks like a threat of dismissal, but it means shot from a gun, as shell fragments are.
explanation.definitionFit: Shell fragments are what an exploding artillery round sends flying, so they are something fired.

clue.text: Put your towel, if not your shirt, on it

definitions.text: Put your towel, if not your shirt, on it

parts.words: Put your towel, if not your shirt, on it
parts.note: a towel can be hung on a wooden drying frame of this name, and to put your shirt on something is to bet everything on it, as on a racing animal

explanation.surface: Advice about where to hang a towel, hinting at a reckless bet.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'put your shirt on' a runner is British slang for staking everything you own on it; a towel ___ is a drying rail.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a towel rail and a racecourse runner share this name, the cryptic hint pointing at both.

clue.text: The done thing

parts.note: usually means proper etiquette, but read literally it is something that has been done or accomplished

explanation.surface: The phrase for socially correct behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The done thing' normally means what is socially proper; here it is read literally as a thing that has been done.
explanation.definitionFit: An accomplishment is literally a deed carried out successfully, a thing done.

clue.text: Gives information which could lead to making an arrest

indicators.note: the words that follow are taken as raw material that could be made into something else, a rearrangement of their letters

explanation.surface: An informer tips off the police, leading to someone being arrested.
explanation.definitionFit: To recount a story is to tell or give an account of it, passing information on.

clue.text: He painted, sculptured and loved in Cairo

indicators.note: to sculpture is to shape material into a new form, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A biography in brief of an artist who painted, sculpted and had a romance in Egypt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sculptured' looks like part of the list of achievements, but it is the anagram signal working on 'and loved in Cairo'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Renaissance master of the Mona Lisa was above all a painter, among his many talents.

clue.text: Nectar may produce a state of ecstasy

indicators.note: the word before is the raw material from which something new may be produced by rearranging it

explanation.surface: Drinking the nectar of the gods can bring on rapture.
explanation.definitionFit: A rapt, dreamlike condition of being carried away is a kind of trance.

clue.text: Tin-opener is cutting into the drink, in fact

indicators.note: the opener of a word is its first letter
one piece cuts into another, splitting it and sitting inside it

parts.note: rum is the classic sailor's drink, often just 'drink' in crosswords

explanation.surface: A tin-opener piercing a can of drink, oddly stated as a fact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tin-opener' looks like a kitchen gadget but means the first letter of 'Tin'.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-evident statement that is obviously so is a fact that hardly needs saying.

clue.text: Egyptian name written in italics

indicators.note: the letters needed are written within the following word, sitting inside it

explanation.surface: An Egyptian's name printed in sloping type.
explanation.definitionFit: Ali is a common Arabic first name, borne by many Egyptians such as Muhammad Ali Pasha.

clue.text: Stock-holder

parts.note: suggests a shareholder in finance, but livestock is also stock, and an enclosure holds it

explanation.surface: A financial investor holding shares.
explanation.walkthrough: In a financial paper 'Stock-holder' suggests shares, but stock here is farm animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Livestock is called stock, and a farm enclosure for cows literally holds that stock.

clue.text: Bow to a lady — it's a sign

parts.note: a bow is a curve, an arc
her refers to a woman, a lady

explanation.surface: Bowing to a lady is a sign of respect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bow' suggests bending at the waist; it is the curved shape. The sign is of the zodiac.
explanation.definitionFit: Sagittarius, the zodiac sign, is pictured as a bowman with drawn bow.

clue.text: They examine the pupils

parts.note: suggests school inspectors testing children, but pupils are also the dark centres of eyes

explanation.surface: Examiners testing schoolchildren.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pupils' suggests schoolchildren, but means the openings at the centre of the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Eye doctors look closely at patients' eyes, including the dark central openings.

clue.text: Wizened prophet in speech

indicators.note: spoken out loud, the word for a prophet matches another word in sound

parts.note: a seer is one who sees the future, a prophet

explanation.surface: A shrivelled old prophet giving an address.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean dried up and withered, as an aged face or autumn leaf may be.

clue.text: Presentation of papa's medal brings a lump to one's throat

indicators.note: the letters are presented in a fresh arrangement, laid out anew

explanation.surface: Seeing dad receive a medal is a moving moment that chokes you up.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the emotional 'lump in the throat'; the definition is literal, the bulge of the larynx.
explanation.definitionFit: The visible bulge of the larynx in the front of the neck is a literal throat lump.

clue.text: Celebration for Father's Day?

parts.note: read whimsically, a festival for a dad (pop) would be a celebration of fathers; the real thing is a music event

explanation.surface: A party to mark the annual day honouring dads.
explanation.walkthrough: Pop is an informal word for father, so the question mark invites reading a music festival as a dads' festival.
explanation.definitionFit: A pop music gala is literally, by the pun, a fete for pops, meaning dads.

clue.text: Clergyman who has always to tear about

indicators.note: the word for tear goes about, around, the word for always

parts.note: to rend is to tear apart
ever means always, as in 'ever hopeful'

explanation.surface: A vicar who is forever charging around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tear' suggests rushing about, but is the verb meaning rip.
explanation.definitionFit: The title given to a minister of the church; a vicar or priest is addressed so.

clue.text: Guidance given by leading journalist exercising caution

parts.note: an editor, abbreviated ED, leads the journalists on a paper

indicators.note: the word is put through exercises, worked into a new shape

explanation.surface: An editor offering careful advice to staff.
explanation.definitionFit: Schooling and instruction are forms of guiding the young, a teaching process.

clue.text: Churchwarden's hose

definitions.meaning: the 's stands for 'is', joining it to the second meaning
a hose is a tube for carrying water, a tube or conduit

explanation.surface: The stockings worn by a parish church official.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hose' suggests stockings worn by the churchwarden; it is a tube. A churchwarden is also an old-style long clay pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a long clay smoking implement and a water tube share this word.

clue.text: Recent stir about an actor's appearance

indicators.note: the mixed-up letters go about, around, the next word
stirring mixes something up, so the word before has its letters mixed

explanation.surface: A fresh commotion over how a performer looks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stir' makes ENTRCE from 'Recent', and 'about' puts it around AN.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor coming onto the stage makes an appearance, the moment of coming in.

clue.text: French priest sought in Lourdes

definitions.meaning: the French word for a parish clergyman, the equivalent of a vicar
Lourdes is a French pilgrimage town where the sick seek miraculous healing

explanation.surface: A priest in France looking for something in the shrine town.
explanation.walkthrough: Lourdes, in southern France, draws pilgrims hoping to be healed at its grotto.
explanation.definitionFit: A French parish clergyman is a curé; healing is what pilgrims at the shrine seek.

clue.text: Where persons may spend time underground

definitions.text: Where persons may spend time underground

parts.words: Where persons may spend time underground
parts.note: describes cells below a castle where prisoners serve their time

explanation.surface: A description of cave dwellers or miners spending hours below the surface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spend time' hints at doing time in prison, in cells below ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Castle prison cells were often below ground, where captives were held for their sentence.

clue.text: A student tells tales but makes friends

parts.note: L is a learner, the plate on a learner driver's car
to tell tales is to tell untruths, to lie

explanation.surface: A dishonest student who somehow still wins people over.
explanation.walkthrough: L stands for learner, from the L-plates British learner drivers display.
explanation.definitionFit: To ally oneself is to join with someone as partner, forming friendly bonds.

clue.text: May I not revel in playing bridge, say?

parts.note: a question like 'can't I?' asking leave, giving CANT and I

indicators.note: the letters are in play, moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone asking if they may not enjoy a game of cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bridge' looks like the card game; it is a structure, of which this projecting beam is a kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A beam fixed at one end only, as used in some bridges, is an example of a structural beam.

clue.text: Duck leaves lake

parts.note: tea leaves are brewed for the drink, so leaves can be tea
L is a standard abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A water bird flies away from a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' looks like a verb, but is the noun, tea leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: A small freshwater dabbling waterfowl, a common species of wild duck.

clue.text: Collected maps of African mountains

definitions.meaning: a mountain range across Morocco, Algeria and Tunisia

explanation.surface: A book of charts showing the peaks of Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: A bound volume of maps, and also a range in north-west Africa, share the name.

clue.text: Parliamentary vote for a large military formation

definitions.meaning: in the UK Parliament, members vote by walking into separate lobbies, a formal split
an army unit of several brigades

explanation.surface: MPs voting on raising a big army unit.
explanation.walkthrough: In the British House of Commons a formal vote is held by MPs dividing into two lobbies.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a formal Commons vote and a big army unit of brigades share this name.

clue.text: Substance that is required to keep cold

indicators.note: one piece must keep, hold within it, another

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: A material needed to keep things chilled.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer, frozen water being what keeps things chilled.
explanation.definitionFit: Frozen water is a solid material, a physical substance.

clue.text: Books with opposing points about love, perhaps

indicators.note: the two compass letters go about, around, the next piece

parts.note: north and south are opposite compass points, N and S

indicators.note: perhaps signals the word may be rearranged into another form

explanation.surface: Books taking opposite views on romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' makes OVEL from 'love', set between N and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Works of long prose fiction are a kind of book.

clue.text: Bays, but can be silent

indicators.note: the word that follows can be turned into another by rearranging its letters

explanation.surface: Coastal bays, though perhaps also quiet places.
explanation.definitionFit: Small arms of the sea reaching into land are coves or small bays.

clue.text: Visionary details I put out

indicators.note: to put out can mean to disturb or upset, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Someone producing a list of particulars.
explanation.definitionFit: A dreamer with lofty ideals is a visionary, seeing how things could be.
